'''Harish Chandra Verma''' (born 3 April 1952), popularly known as '''HCV''', is an Indian [[experimental physicist]], author and [[emeritus professor]] of the [[Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur]]. He wrote the book "Concepts of Physics." In 2021, he was awarded the [[Padma Shri]], the fourth highest civilian award, by the [[Government of India]] for his contribution to Physics Education.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.dashboard-padmaawards.gov.in/?Year=2020-2020|title=Padma Awards {{!}} Interactive Dashboard|website=www.dashboard-padmaawards.gov.in|language=en|access-date=26 January 2020|archive-date=1 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220201172057/http://www.dashboard-padmaawards.gov.in/?Year=2020-2020|url-status=dead}}</ref> His field of research is [[nuclear physics]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://iitk.ac.in/new/h-c-verma | title=Profile of DR. H. C. Verma | publisher=Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur | access-date=2 April 2016}}</ref>

He has authored several school, undergraduate and graduate level textbooks. He has been awarded the [[Abul Kalam Azad|Maulana Abul Kalam Azad]] Shiksha Puruskar by the [[Bihar]] [[Government of Bihar|state government]].<ref name="Hindustan">{{cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/education/meet-padma-shri-hc-verma-who-struggled-to-pass-exam-in-school-but-teaches-india-physics-today/story-tRRdohVIk4sxGDpKti8wtL.html|title=Meet Padma Shri HC Verma, who struggled to pass in school, teaches India Physics today
|publisher=[[Hindustan Times]]|date=10 February 2020}}</ref><ref name="Azad">{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/bihar/azad-honour-for-physics-teacher/cid/1368629|title=Azad honour for physics teacher|publisher=The Telegraph|date=11 November 2017}}</ref>

==Early life and study==
Verma was born on 3 April 1952 to Ganesh Prasad Verma, a teacher and Ramvati Verma in [[Darbhanga]], [[Bihar]]. He obtained his [[Bachelor of Science]] (B. Sc) degree at [[Patna Science College]]. Then he obtained [[Master of Science]] (M. Sc) and [[Doctor of Philosophy]] (Ph. D) at [[IIT Kanpur]].<ref name="Deccan" />

==Career==

===Patna Science College===
In early 1980, Verma joined Patna Science College as a lecturer.<ref name=Hindustan /> He remained at the college as a lecturer and reader for 15 years<ref name=Azad /> before resigning from the college and joining IIT Kanpur.

===IIT Kanpur===
Verma joined IIT Kanpur in 1994 as an assistant professor. Here he pursued research in experimental [[nuclear physics]]. He has published 139 research papers.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Verma|first1=H C|url=https://www.hcverma.in/ReadMore|website=H C Verma|access-date=10 April 2018|title=Prof. H C Verma}}</ref> He retired on 30 June 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/education/iit-kanpur-hc-verma-retires-concepts-of-physics-textbooks-students-pour-adoration-on-twitter-4733345/|title=IIT Kanpur's HC Verma retires, students pour adoration on Twitter|publisher=[[The Indian Express]]|date=3 July 2017}}</ref>

===Physics outreach===
[[File:President Kovind presents Padma Shri to Dr Harish Chandra Verma for Science and Engineering.jpg|alt=HC Verma receiving Padma Shri from the President of India at Rashtrapati Bhavan|thumb|HC Verma receiving Padma Shri from the [[President of India]] at [[Rashtrapati Bhavan]]|393x393px]]
Verma has developed more than six hundred ‘low cost’ physics experiments that teachers can employ in their classrooms. In 2011, he set up the National Anveshika Network of India (NANI), a flagship program of the [[Indian Association of Physics Teachers]] (IAPT). He is the national coordinator for this program. There are currently 22 Anveshikas in the country.<ref name=Hindustan /><ref name="Deccan">{{cite web|url=https://www.deccanchronicle.com/lifestyle/viral-and-trending/060618/meet-the-man-who-taught-india-physics.html|title=Meet the man who taught India physics|publisher=[[Deccan Chronicle]]|date=6 June 2018}}</ref>[https://iitkalumni.org/daa]
